Sam, Hannah —

Brief technical estimate below (high-level, happy to run your traces if you want exact numbers). Assumptions: base model perf = 100k tokens/day, avg request length = 250 tokens (50 prompt + 200 generation), steady-state latency SLO = 150ms (p50), baseline no-cache unquantized throughput = X tokens/sec on our hosted service. Savings are illustrative.

1) Prefix / KV caching
- Expected hit-rate scenarios: 30% / 60% / 80%
- Effective saved generation tokens on hit: ~65% of generation tokens (we conservatively exclude prompt tokens)
- Estimated cost delta vs baseline: 30% hit -> ~12% cost reduction; 60% hit -> ~24% reduction; 80% -> ~33% reduction.

2) 4-bit quantization (post-quant-aware tuning)
- Typical token-level throughput gains: 1.6x–2.2x depending on model and custom kernels. We recommend per-model calibration (we can run a short micro-benchmark).
- Cost reduction estimate if safe to deploy quantized weights: ~35%–50% additional, but caveats: (a) slight latency variance p99 on older GPUs, (b) potential minimal drop in generation quality on some instruction-following prompts — we recommend a 1-week eval run.

3) Combined impact (cache + quant)
- Combined conservative estimate (60% cache hit + 4-bit quant): ~50%–60% unit-cost reduction. In many customer pilots we observed 45% as a conservative operating number after accounting for cache cold starts and QC tuning.

Operational notes / guardrails:
- Start pilot with cache enabled, default TTL 24h and adaptive refresh for hot prefixes. That gets immediate win with minimal product changes.
- Run 4-bit quantization in a staged canary (10% traffic) with automated quality checks on a small eval prompt set (we provide the eval harness).
- We can enable automatic fallback to unquantized model if quality/regression thresholds are tripped.

Attachment: Pilot_SOW_Draft.docx (stub)

If you want, send a representative trace (anonymized) and I'll run a short benchmark with our quant kernels and give a per-day cost estimate.

-Karthik
